bib.title: Model-Agnostic Meta-Learning for Fast Adaptation of Deep Networks

question: Can a model be trained so that a few gradient steps on a few examples of a new task give good performance, in a way that works for any gradient-trained model and for classification, regression and RL?
hypothesis: Training the initial parameters so that one or a few gradient steps on a new task generalise well yields a representation that is easy and fast to fine-tune.
contributions: A simple model- and task-agnostic meta-learning algorithm (MAML) that trains initial parameters for fast gradient-based adaptation
Demonstration across few-shot regression, image classification and policy-gradient RL
State-of-the-art or comparable few-shot classification with no extra learned parameters

method.summary: MAML meta-trains initial parameters theta by sampling a batch of tasks, taking one or more inner gradient steps on K examples per task, and updating theta by the gradient of the post-update loss on fresh task data (second-order through the inner step, or first-order approximation). Evaluated on sinusoid regression, Omniglot and MiniImagenet few-shot classification, and rllab RL tasks.

datasets.name: Sinusoid regression
datasets.size: tasks sampled continuously; K=10 datapoints per task in training, K in {5,10,20} at test
datasets.split: amplitude in [0.1, 5.0], phase in [0, pi]; x uniform in [-5.0, 5.0]

datasets.name: Omniglot
datasets.split: 1200 characters random for training irrespective of alphabet, remaining for testing
datasets.preprocessing: images downsampled to 28 x 28; augmented with rotations by multiples of 90 degrees

datasets.name: rllab 2D navigation, half-cheetah and ant (MuJoCo)
datasets.size: task distributions: goal position in unit square; goal velocity 0.0-2.0 (cheetah), 0.0-3.0 (ant); forward/backward direction
datasets.preprocessing: ant goal velocity: positive reward bonus per timestep

models.name: Sinusoid regressor
models.architecture: MLP, 2 hidden layers of size 40, ReLU

models.name: Conv classifier (Omniglot/MiniImagenet)
models.architecture: 4 modules of 3x3 conv with 64 filters, batch norm, ReLU, 2x2 max-pool, then softmax

other.omniglot: strided convolutions instead of max-pooling; last hidden layer dim 64

models.name: Non-conv classifier (Omniglot)
models.architecture: MLP with 4 hidden layers 256,128,64,64, batch norm and ReLU, then linear and softmax

models.name: RL policy
models.architecture: MLP, 2 hidden layers of size 100, ReLU

training.objective: meta-objective: sum over tasks of L_Ti(f_theta'_i) where theta'_i = theta - alpha grad L_Ti(f_theta); MSE for regression, cross-entropy for classification, negative expected reward (REINFORCE) for RL
training.optimizer: Adam as meta-optimizer for regression (alpha fixed 0.01); classification meta-optimizer not stated in text; TRPO as meta-optimizer for RL
training.lr: inner alpha: 0.01 (sinusoid), 0.4 (Omniglot 5-way), 0.1 (Omniglot 20-way), 0.01 (MiniImagenet), 0.1 first step then 0.05 (RL); meta step size beta not stated
training.batch_size: meta batch: 32 tasks (Omniglot 5-way), 16 (20-way), 4 and 2 (MiniImagenet 1-shot and 5-shot), 20 (2D nav), 40 (locomotion); inner batch N*K examples
training.hardware: single NVIDIA Pascal Titan X GPU (classification)

other.inner_steps_train_test: Omniglot 5-way: 1 train / 3 test; 20-way: 5 / 5; MiniImagenet: 5 train / 10 test; sinusoid: 1 train; RL: 1 train, up to 4 at test
other.RL: horizon 100 (nav), 200 (locomotion); 20 trajectories per step (40 for ant fwd/back, 40 samples per step at nav test); linear feature baseline; best-average-return model during training used; finite differences for Hessian-vector products in TRPO
other.meta_eval_examples: 15 examples per class for post-update meta-gradient on MiniImagenet
other.first_order: drops Hessian-vector backward pass, about 33% faster

inference.samples: classification: 95% confidence intervals over tasks (number of test tasks not stated); sinusoid K in {5,10,20} points; RL: up to 4 gradient updates of 40 samples (nav)

metrics.name: N-way K-shot accuracy
metrics.definition: classify new instances of N unseen classes after adaptation on K examples per class

metrics.name: MSE (sinusoid)
metrics.definition: mean squared error after k gradient steps on K points

metrics.name: Average return (RL)
metrics.definition: mean reward after k policy-gradient updates

baselines: Pretraining on all tasks then fine-tune
eval.protocol: Tasks held out at meta-test; Vinyals et al. 2016 N-way protocol; Omniglot split may not be strictly comparable to prior work; MiniImagenet baselines taken from Ravi & Larochelle

results.claim: MAML reaches 98.7% 5-way 1-shot and 99.9% 5-shot accuracy on held-out Omniglot characters, narrowly above prior methods.
results.setup: Omniglot, conv model, 1200 train characters, 95% CI over tasks

results.claim: On MiniImagenet MAML scores 48.70% 5-way 1-shot, versus 43.44% for the meta-learner LSTM.
results.setup: MiniImagenet test classes, 4-layer conv 32 filters, 5 inner steps train / 10 test, alpha 0.01

results.claim: On MiniImagenet 5-shot MAML scores 63.11% versus 60.60% for the meta-learner LSTM.
First-order approximation nearly matches full MAML on MiniImagenet 1-shot.
results.table: Table 1, row MAML, first order approx., 5-way 1-shot

results.claim: Dropping the second-order term gives about a 33% speed-up.
results.setup: first-order MAML versus full MAML network computation

results.claim: On 5-shot sinusoid regression, MAML after 1 gradient step has MSE 0.67 versus 2.41 for pretraining on all tasks.
results.setup: sinusoid, 5 test points, 1 gradient step; MAML 0.38 at 5 steps, 0.35 at 10 steps; pretrain 2.23, 2.19

results.claim: Averaging in parameter space (multi-task) did worse than pretraining on all tasks on sinusoid regression.
results.setup: 5-shot, 1 step, multi-task no reg; 500 separate models averaged
results.table: Table 2, row multi-task, no reg, column 1

results.claim: On half-cheetah forward/backward MAML reaches average return 293.19 after one gradient step; context vector stays negative.
results.setup: half-cheetah, 1 gradient step; MAML 0 steps -50.69, 2 steps 313.48, 3 steps 315.65

results.claim: A context-vector adaptation baseline reaches 94.9% on 5-way 1-shot Omniglot, below MAML's 98.7%.
results.setup: Omniglot, free input vector z adapted instead of weights

results.claim: MAML-trained model keeps improving with more gradient steps though trained for one step.
results.quote: MAML continues to improve with additional gradient steps without overﬁtting

results.claim: In RL pretraining is in some cases worse than random initialisation, while MAML initialisation adapts in two or three gradient steps.
results.quote: pretraining is in some cases worse than random initialization

limits: Few-shot tasks are small supervised or simulated-control problems; no large pretrained or language models.
Second-order meta-gradient is costly; the authors only test a first-order approximation on MiniImagenet.
Omniglot results may not be strictly comparable because prior train/test splits were unavailable.
RL needs fresh on-policy samples for each adaptation step.
Meta step size beta, classification meta-optimizer, seeds and number of test tasks are not stated.

terms.definition: the model learns a new task from only K samples and feedback from that task
compatible with any model trained with gradient descent
